The email arrived on a Tuesday, nestled amongst bills and newsletters, a splash of school colors against the muted grey of his inbox. "St. Augustine’s 20th Reunion – Volunteers Needed!" it proclaimed, the font a cheerful, if slightly outdated, serif. Noel almost deleted it without a second thought. Twenty years. A lifetime, it felt, since he’d last walked those hallowed, and occasionally mildewy, halls. 

He hesitated. The subject line, however, continued to nag. St. Augustine's had been… formative. Not always in the best ways, admittedly, but formative nonetheless. He’d learned a surprising amount about resilience, about navigating social hierarchies, and about the peculiar scent of old gym socks. And, he supposed, he was looking for something to fill the quiet evenings lately. The freelance writing gigs were sporadic, and the cat, Bartholomew, was growing increasingly demanding of his attention. 

Clicking the link, he found a surprisingly well-designed website – a far cry from the pixelated Geocities pages of his youth. There were testimonials from previous reunion attendees, a gallery of grainy yearbook photos, and a volunteer sign-up form. Categories included Decorations, Music, Food & Beverage, and “General Assistance.” Noel considered “General Assistance.” It sounded… vague. Safe. He could alphabetize nametags, probably. 

He scrolled further, past the meticulously crafted timeline of school events and the section devoted to “Remembering Those We’ve Lost.” A wave of unexpected sadness washed over him. Faces flickered in his mind – faces of classmates, teachers, even the perpetually grumpy cafeteria lady, Mrs. Henderson. They were all older now, scattered across the country, leading lives he could only vaguely imagine. 

With a sigh, he clicked the box next to "Decorations." He’d always had a knack for spatial arrangement, for making a room feel… right. It was a skill he’d honed over the years, decorating his small apartment with a curated collection of vintage finds and Bartholomew’s strategically placed cat toys. Maybe he could bring that same sensibility to the St. Augustine’s gymnasium.

The confirmation email arrived instantly. "Welcome, Volunteer Noel Harding! We’re thrilled to have you on board." He reread it, a strange mixture of apprehension and anticipation swirling within him. He hadn't spoken to anyone from St. Augustine’s in… well, a very long time. He wondered who would be there. He wondered if anyone would even remember him. 



He glanced at Bartholomew, who was currently attempting to scale the curtains. "Looks like we're going to a reunion, buddy," he murmured to the cat. Bartholomew blinked, unimpressed, and resumed his ascent.
